modify.note: When a signup carries a team/org invite token, both calcomHandler and selfHostedHandler check whether a user with the invited email already exists before creating the account; if one does, they stop and return a 409 'user already exists' error instead of continuing the signup flow. Signups with an invite token for a new email, and signups without a token, behave as before.

add_nodes.label: Signup fetch client
add_nodes.summary: Client-side module that posts signup data to the signup API and returns a typed result.
add_nodes.description: Replaces the inline signup fetch logic used by the signup form. Wraps the request with proper error handling and shared signup error codes, so callers can tell a user-already-exists response and a checkout-session response apart from other failures.
add_nodes.note: Move the signup request out of the signup form into this module. It must never throw on a bad response: an unreadable server response is reported as an invalid-server-response error, and a 409 is recognised as user-already-exists. When the signup form gets user-already-exists for an invite token, it shows a translated toast telling the user they already have an account and redirects them to the login page.

add_edges.label: posts signup request
add_edges.note: Sends the signup data (including any invite token and Turnstile token) to the signup API and turns the response, including the 409 user-already-exists case, into a result the form can act on.
